meta.name: SR22T G7+ Hot Start Procedure
meta.verified: 2026-07-11 | AFM + COPA Community + Jason Price (Platinum CSIP CFI II)

section.name: Oil Temperature Determination
section.description: Hot start technique depends on oil temperature, NOT elapsed time since shutdown.
section.item: Use normal start technique
Try hot start first; fall back to normal if unsuccessful
Hot start technique required

section.name: Technique A: Mixture Advance During Crank (AFM-Based)
section.description: More hands-on; requires practice. Best for high-altitude/high-temp scenarios (Sedona, etc.)

subsection.name: Start Setup
subsection.item: FULL LEAN (or nearly closed for very warm engine)
1/4 to 3/4 forward (start at 1/4; less is often better)

subsection.name: Crank & Start
subsection.item: Release starter, retard power to ~1000 RPM

subsection.name: After Start
subsection.item: Lean until RPM peaks, leave it there

section.name: Technique B: Simpler AFM-Aligned Method (Field-Proven ~99% Reliability)
section.description: Simpler; less coordination needed. Works nearly 100% when followed correctly. Recommended for most pilots/conditions.

subsection.name: Crank & Start
subsection.item: PRESS AT FIRST INDICATION OF FUEL FLOW

subsection.name: Critical After-Start Step
subsection.item: If engine momentarily stumbles (NORMAL—engine recovers on own)
Normal as vapor flows through system; leave throttle alone
During stumble will cause engine shutdown

section.name: Critical Points (All Techniques)
section.item: Engine must show rising oil pressure within 30 seconds of start. If no pressure rise after 60 seconds in cold weather, shut down and troubleshoot.
Start with 1/4 to 1/2 open depending on technique. If engine fires and power is high, pull back immediately to prevent surge.
Newer aircraft come with robust starters. Upgrades not required for G7+.

section.name: Flooded Engine Recovery
section.description: Signs: Weak intermittent firing, black smoke from exhaust, strong fuel smell.
section.item: OFF
5–10 seconds for fuel to drain
FULL LEAN
FULL FORWARD
CRANK 10–15 seconds
Starter RELEASE, Power RETARD to ~1000 RPM, Mixture SLOWLY advance
ON
~1000 RPM; cool down before attempting flight

section.name: Troubleshooting
section.item: Check: Battery charge, fuel pump ON, mixture not CUTOFF, starter disconnect not engaged
Battery low? Oil cold/thick? Wait for engine to warm slightly.
Engine Knob BOTH (not one mag), verify fuel pump on, try alternate power setting (1/4 vs 3/4), oil temp correct?
Oil pressure rising? Engine cold—normal as engine warms. Monitor for smooth rise to 35–45 PSI.
NORMAL—do not touch throttle. Engine will recover on its own.
